jobs.description:
Are you curious how your favorite ice cream is produced – and interested in developing training that can help others understand as well?
At Gram Equipment, we are looking for a student worker to our Gram Equipment Academy team, where we develop high-quality online training on our ice cream processing equipment – for internal as well as external use.

Your primary responsibility will be to translate our existing trainings into German learning experiences, review and update existing trainings and contribute to the development of new training.

You will have the opportunity to get in-depth knowledge about how the specific machine contributes to the production of ice cream, and turn it into training, that is understandable for machine operators from customer sites all around the world. 

This will require that you focus on:
• German translation. Your main focus will be to transform existing English training into clear, engaging and technically accurate German content.
• Project management.: You will get full responsibility for managing your own projects according to the goals, we set together, and we will have short weekly follow ups to coordinate your progress. 
• Stakeholder collaboration. You will have to coordinate and meet with colleagues from across the organization to gather knowledge and feedback that ensures that the training includes all important aspects and addresses the needs of both customers and your colleagues.
• Follow and bring new ideas to the existing process for developing training. The process stretches from gathering knowledge, through writing a script and finding visuals, to developing the training using text, pictures, videos and other interactive elements.
• Content creation. You will have to use creativity and writing skills to produce engaging and effective online training for our customers, using our authoring tool Genially. Templates and previous trainings are available for support and inspiration. 
• Quality Assurance. Ensure that the training is correct, of high quality and that the user experience is consistent. 
• Support the continuous development of Gram Equipment Academy.

Though you will have to work independently, we consider it a team effort to be able to provide training, so support and sparring are always within arm’s length. In general, our team is characterized by an optimistic atmosphere and an informal, humoristic tone.

We do not have any specific requirements for your education. However, we are working with technically complex ice cream processing equipment, so it will be an advantage if you either have some technical understanding of machines and processes – or at least a strong curiosity and willingness to learn.

You must also have an interest in and capabilities for developing the learning material and ensuring its quality. 

In addition, we do require the following:
• Personality: A self-driven team player with an optimistic and proactive work attitude and strong interpersonal communication skills – since you must be able to collaborate with colleagues from across the organization.
• Creative thinking: We appreciate input that drives change and that has the potential to improve our content, as well as the way we work.
• Language: Our company language is English. So, you must be able to communicate in English, both spoken and written, including the mediation of technical aspects. In addition, German language skills are essential, and you must be able to write clear German and handle technical terminology with precision.
• Skills: Some technical understanding of equipment, graphic capabilities and a visual eye for the detail.
• Work approach: Self-driven, proactive, flexible, structured, and quality-focused. 

We expect the average working hours to be 10 to 15 per week, preferably in the office for the purpose of collaboration, but also for the social aspect. The date of employment and your hour distribution will be adapted to your studies.

The position is located at our main office in Kolding, where you will find an informal atmosphere between good and dedicated colleagues. 

Application:
Please send your application and CV as soon as possible. Feel free to add any other relevant attachments showing your past work. If you have any questions for the position, please do not hesitate to reach out to Learning & Development Specialist, Cristian Buita on +45 20 82 02 64 or CRBU@gram-equipment.com, or Business Developer Teamlead, Line Andersen on +45 53 66 74 21 or LSAN@gram-equipment.com.

Gram Equipment A/S offers 

Gram Equipment A/S is the global leading supplier of advanced equipment and process installations for industrial ice production. With an extensive global network of subsidiaries, agents, sales- and service offices and around 600 employees worldwide, Gram Equipment has the optimal base for fulfilling our customers’ demands. 

The company is constantly striving to extend the portfolio of innovative solutions. We aim to ensure that our customers always can react fast to the demands from their customers and consumers worldwide. 

Our vision: We ensure our customers’ success in the ice cream industry by providing innovative solutions and services, while seeking to minimize the environmental impact of our solutions and footprint.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Moiré and Patterned 2D Materials for Bandgap Engineering - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
If you want to design the electronic properties of a material rather than simply measure them, this PhD puts the tools in your hands. When two-dimensional crystals are stacked with a controlled twist, or when a periodic pattern is imprinted into them, an artificial superlattice emerges in which the band structure can be reshaped and bandgaps opened by design, using a novel combination of 2D materials and freestanding oxide membranes. 

You will create such materials yourself in a group that has worked with 2D materials for two decades and with full access to the cleanroom and microscopy infrastructure at DTU Nanolab. The project is part of METRIQS and is carried out together with national and international partners.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to create and control superlattices in graphene and other 2D materials, and to establish how the engineered structure translates into an engineered electronic band structure. You will pursue two complementary routes: assembling hybrid van der Waals heterostructures in which the moiré periodicity is set by twist angle and lattice mismatch and imprinting periodic patterns directly into the 2D material or its supporting layers by nanofabrication. Both routes call for careful design, reproducible processing and close comparison between intended and realised structure. You will work with colleagues at DTU Physics and DTU Nanolab and with partners in the METRIQS collaboration. 

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Design superlattice geometries and device layouts, using modelling and simulation to decide what is worth fabricating.
• Assemble hybrid van der Waals heterostructures from graphene, hBN, transition metal dichalcogenides and related materials with controlled twist and alignment, using a newly developed semi-automatic stacking system, and collect data on stacking recipes and results to obtain and document optimal parameters through datamining and statistics. 
• Imprint periodic patterns into 2D materials and their supporting layers using electron beam lithography, etching, thin film deposition and related nanofabrication.
• Fabricate devices in which the engineered materials can be contacted, gated and measured.
• Characterise structure and electronic properties by scanning probe microscopies, electron microscopies, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy and electrical transport at cryogenic temperatures. 
• Connect the measured electronic response back to the intended superlattice design, and iterate on the design.
• Establish reproducible fabrication and measurement protocols, analyse your data and present the results in publications and at conferences.
We are looking for a candidate with a background in physics, nanotechnology, materials science, electrical engineering or a related field. You should have hands-on experience with micro- or nanofabrication or comparable experimental laboratory work, and be comfortable with systematic work, data analysis and programming for design, automation or modelling. Experience with 2D materials, layout and CAD design, electron microscopy or electronic transport is an advantage, but the project spans several techniques, and we do not expect you to bring all of them with you. We value curiosity, persistence and the ambition to take ownership of your own project.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Peter Bøggild and Timothy John Booth. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is 1 January 2027, or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Professor Peter Bøggild, pbog@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU Physics and DTU Nanolab at https://physics.dtu.dk/ and www.nanolab.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 1 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Physics conducts research across a broad range of fundamental and applied physics. The position will be based in the department's 2D Materials Physics and Engineering section (2DPHYS), where we study the synthesis, fabrication and physical properties of atomically thin materials and heterostructures, including also hybrid heterostructures. The project makes extensive use of the nanofabrication and characterisation facilities at DTU Nanolab and involves close collaboration with national and international research partners in METRIQS.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced financial-crime leader to be our registered MLRO / Hvidvaskansvarlig (HVL § 7, stk. 2) for Monta Pay ApS under our EMI license and to lead Financial Crime Prevention (FCP) across Monta, group-wide for the Danish/EEA EMI plus UK and US compliance as those markets scale. The role is registered with Finanstilsynet, so the appointment is subject to a fit & proper assessment as a change of key function holder.

Monta Pay ApS holds an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) license, granted by Finanstilsynet in April 2026. We are now migrating our financial services from Monta ApS to Monta Pay ApS, with go-live planned for Q2 2027. This is the moment the AML/FCP framework moves from build to live operation, and you will own it.

This is a high-profile, senior role. You sit at the centre of our financial-services compliance strategy as we scale, "directly exposed to the fire." You must balance obligations against resources with a risk-based approach, communicate complex issues clearly to senior leaders and the Board, and run your work-streams with strong, solution-oriented project management. In return, you have an outsized impact on how Monta builds and operates financial services compliance, and direct exposure to decision-making at a fast-growing scale-up.

You report day to day to Nick Skovsen, COO of Monta Pay ApS, with direct, independent access to the CEO and executive management of Monta Pay ApS and to its Board and Governance, Risk & Compliance Committee.

Key responsibilities

• 
Registered MLRO / Hvidvaskansvarlig: Act as the statutory AML-responsible person for Monta Pay under the EMI license. Approve AML/CTF policies and high-risk customer relationships escalated by the first line (PEPs, and business involving high-risk third countries). Receive internal escalations, decide on and file SARs/STRs with the FIU, and be the primary AML contact for Finanstilsynet.

• 
Own the Financial Crime Prevention framework: Steward Monta's FCP model (our nine-pillar "FC9" framework) covering AML/CFT, sanctions, fraud, and anti-bribery & corruption. Propose the risk appetite and risk-based approach for Board approval and monitor against it, and keep the framework effective and proportionate to our activities, customer types (B2B & B2C), and transaction flows.

• 
Fraud, transaction monitoring & customer due diligence: Own the frameworks for fraud prevention, transaction monitoring, and KYC/KYB (CDD/EDD, PEP and sanctions screening) across onboarding and the lifecycle (EU and US). Set the rules, thresholds and procedures the Financial Operations team runs in the first line, and assure their quality and effectiveness.

• 
Sanctions & screening: Set the screening standards (lists, thresholds, re-screening frequency) and assure the quality of first-line alert handling.

• 
Policy suite, risk assessment & governance: Maintain the AML/CFT policy suite in the Centralised Policy Register (with version control and Board-approval tracking), and own the Business-Wide Risk Assessment (BWRA) and the AML risk assessment underpinning the framework.

• 
Regulatory reporting: Deliver AML and payments regulatory reporting (for example Section 99 Payment Act, KPSD, AML/CTF returns) and ensure CESOP readiness.

• 
Technology, controls & assurance: Work with Product and Engineering on case management, screening and monitoring tooling and AI/automation, oversee AML-relevant third parties, and run the internal-controls framework (monitoring, QA, remediation).

• 
Training, culture & Board liaison: Build AML/FCP training and a strong compliance culture, and advise Senior Management and the Board GRC Committee on financial-crime risk, regulatory change, and performance.

• 
Build and lead the team: Build out and lead the second-line FCP/AML team as volumes grow post go-live.

What You’ll Walk Into (first 6 to 12 months)

• 
The foundations are in place; the job is to make them operational for go-live.

• 
On AML: everything required to obtain the EMI license has been submitted and approved. The remaining gap is operational readiness, and that is the focus: embedding the framework in day-to-day operations and rolling it out with our customers and with colleagues across Monta.

• 
On FCP: This role brings centralised ownership and direction, consolidating what already exists, formalising it into clear Standard Operating Procedures, and training the relevant teams on them ahead of go-live.

• 
Concrete early priorities include standing up transaction monitoring and fraud detection, locking v1.0 of the policy suite (Sanctions, PEP, EDD, Outsourcing, and the Sanction-Screening and SAR/STR filing SOPs) into the Centralised Policy Register, building the regulatory-reporting data structure and CESOP readiness, finalising KYC/KYB (EU + US), and securing your Finanstilsynet fit & proper approval ahead of go-live. A structured focus-areas plan accompanies this role.

Requirements

• 
Minimum 3 years (ideally 5+, given this is a registered key-function role) of relevant experience in the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, ideally in a licensed EMI, payment institution, bank, or regulated fintech. Comparable experience in public authorities, AML consulting, or other AML-regulated sectors (for example gaming/gambling) will also be considered.

• 
Strong, current understanding of Danish AML law (Hvidvaskloven) and the EU framework (AMLD/AMLR, EBA guidelines), plus sanctions regimes. Awareness of the incoming EU AML package (AMLR + AMLD6, applying July 2027) is a plus.

•

Hands-on experience with fraud prevention and transaction monitoring, and with the underlying tooling (KYC/KYB, screening, monitoring, case management). Data literacy and comfort with AI/automation are a plus.

• 
Experience across risk controls, compliance, the payments area, credit management, or lines-of-defence leadership. Fintech/scale-up experience is a plus.

• 
Strong communication skills, autonomy, and sound decision-making, with the ability to build from a blank page and then scale a function and team.

Analytical and investigative skills to detect patterns and anomalies in financial transactions and to investigate suspicious activity.

• 
Danish speaking, or willing to learn (the role is regulator-facing).

• 
Relevant education (economics, mathematics, law, or financial-sector training) is a plus.

• 
No prior convictions or legal issues that would make the candidate unfit for the role, particularly offences related to financial crime, fraud, money laundering, or other criminal activities undermining trust and integrity.

If this sounds like you, we look forward to receiving your application.

The project focuses on the development of next-generation quantum-enhanced algorithms for predicting the electronic excited-state properties of organic molecules. By integrating quantum chemistry, quantum computing, and computational materials design, the project aims to enable the efficient screening and discovery of sustainable materials for solar energy conversion and other clean-energy technologies. The PhD project is a collaborative effort between Sonia Coriani (DTU Chemistry, principal supervisor), Piotr de Silva (DTU Energy Conversion and Storage, co-supervisor), and Achintya Kumar Dutta (IIT Bombay, co-supervisor), and is cofinanced through a DTU Alliance PhD fellowship and the Novo Nordisk Foundation-funded Hybrid Quantum Chemistry on Hybrid Quantum Computers (HQC)² project.

As part of the Alliance partnership, the PhD student is expected to spend two research stays of approximately three months each (or one stay of 6 months) at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, working under the supervision of Achintya Kumar Dutta and collaborating closely with a PhD student based at IIT Bombay. The project will also involve close interaction with the research teams associated with the (HQC)² project, providing access to a broad international network and expertise at the interface of quantum chemistry and quantum computing. 

Responsibilities and qualifications

• Design computational methods for predicting excited-state properties, in particular algorithms suitable for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) and Early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
• Generate high-quality benchmark datasets
• Implement computational software and workflows
• Use developed algorithms to: screen candidate organic molecules, support inverse molecular design, discover sustainable energy materials for next-generation solar-energy technologies 
• Disseminate the results of the research in scientific articles and at conferences 
• Participate in the group meetings and activities
• Teaching-related activities at the Department of Chemistry, Technical University of Denmark, including (co)supervision of BSc and MSc student projects
The following additional qualifications are considered as a boon:

• Solid mathematical background and experience within quantum chemistry, computational spectroscopy and programming in Fortran and/or C/C++ and/or Python
• Experience in the development and implementation of correlated wavefunction methods of quantum chemistry, for instance Coupled Cluster or multireference methods.
• Experience on the development of quantum computing algorithms for NISQ and/or (early) Fault Tolerant quantum computers
• Experience with quantum computing software libraries like IBM’s Qiskit or Pennylane
Equally important, you are highly motivated, able to work independently and confident in both written and spoken English. You strive towards scientific excellence, are ambitious and hard working. You enjoy collaborating with others from diverse backgrounds as well as supporting more junior group members. Only applicants, who seek to be among the brightest in their field and do science at the highest international level, will be considered

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree, in either Chemistry (preferably with a focus on theoretical and computational chemistry), Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or Quantum Information Science.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by a panel composed by Prof. Coriani, Prof. De Silva and Assoc. Prof. Kumar Dutta.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position.

The position is available with start on January 1, 2027 or as soon as possible after 01/01/2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Enquires about the position may be made to Professor Sonia Coriani, soco@kemi.dtu.dk 

You can read more about DTU Chemistry at www.kemi.dtu.dk, and about Coriani’s group at https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/Research/Physical-Chemistry/sonia-coriani-group

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• List of publications (if any), including the master and bachelor theses
• List of up to three scientists with whom you have closely worked in your past research, whom we may contact for references
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Chemistry is an internationally leading institute with research and teaching in the main areas of chemistry: physical (incl. theoretical/computational), biophysical, organic and inorganic chemistry. Academic excellence, innovation and entrepreneurship are core to its research activities, and drivers of academic and industrial collaborations, spinouts, and high impact publications. The Department has a long-standing tradition of training PhD students and Postdoc fellows who move on to successful careers within academia and industry.

The department actively contributes to both basic chemical research and applied research in energy, pharmaceuticals, catalysis and materials. Strong relationships exist with neighbouring areas such as physics, nanotechnology, biochemistry, including collaboration with industry and universities at home and abroad. Many research projects are also closely linked to applications. The institute has approx. 180 employees.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

**Product Management at Dalux, Innovating the Construction Industry

**Dalux continues to grow rapidly, and we’re looking for a Product Manager to help shape the future of BIM and make complex building information accessible and useful to everyone in construction.

As a Product Manager at Dalux, you’ll operate at the intersection of customer needs, technology, and business strategy. You’ll take ownership of the product roadmap and collaborate closely with Product Design and Development teams to deliver intuitive, high-performing BIM experiences.

You’ll play a key role in evolving how our users view, navigate, understand, and collaborate around building models. Combining an understanding of BIM, UI/UX, and computer graphics, you’ll help turn complex technical capabilities into tools that work effortlessly for our users.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Product Discovery: Evaluate and prioritize new product opportunities, balancing user value, technical feasibility, and business impact.

• Customer Insights: Work closely with users to understand their BIM workflows, uncover pain points, and translate feedback into meaningful product improvements.

• User Experience: Collaborate with Product Design to make complex BIM interactions intuitive, from navigating 3D models to finding and understanding building information.

• BIM and Visualization: Work with engineers on model visualization and interaction, balancing visual quality, responsiveness, and performance when handling large and complex building models.

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Align with engineers, designers, and fellow product managers to deliver cohesive experiences across Dalux products.

• Feature Ownership: Lead new features from discovery and definition through development, delivery, and validation with users.

• Product Strategy: Help define the direction of BIM at Dalux, identifying opportunities and deciding where we should invest to deliver the greatest value.

**What To Expect As a Daluxian

**At Dalux, we offer a creative, collaborative, and supportive environment where your ideas make an impact. Here’s what you can look forward to as part of our team:

• A central location in Copenhagen, a focus on work/life balance, and no dress code.

• An active social environment with monthly events and social clubs.

• A flat organization with open communication, a short path from idea to product, and the creative freedom and trust to create tangible value for our users.

• A highly specialized, international team with room for creativity and professional growth.

• A strong focus on diversity and inclusion, where your ideas are heard and opportunities are available to all.

• Attractive employee benefits, including health insurance, a lunch plan, coffee and fruit, free fitness facilities, and free parking.

• Support for your professional development and personal well-being.

**About You

**We believe you have a solid background in product management and experience working closely with software development teams, preferably on SaaS platforms. You’re curious about how technology works and motivated by making sophisticated tools easy to use.

We also believe you:

• Have 5+ years of experience in product management, taking products or features from discovery to delivery.

• Have a background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Understand BIM workflows and how building models and their data are used across design, construction, and operations.

• Have a strong understanding of UI/UX principles and can work with designers to evaluate interaction flows, challenge unnecessary complexity, and validate solutions with users.

• Have a working understanding of computer graphics concepts such as 3D geometry, rendering, and model interaction, enabling you to discuss technical trade-offs with engineers.

• Can balance strategic thinking with attention to detail, particularly where usability, model complexity, and performance meet.

• Are comfortable working in agile development environments and prioritizing based on user insights and product outcomes.

• Communicate clearly and fluently in English, both written and spoken.

Experience with IFC, BIM viewers, or other software for working with 3D models would be an advantage.

**Ready for the next step?

**If we have managed to pique your interest, we would love to hear from you. Send us your motivated CV and an application.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your application today.

**About Dalux

**Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics. Despite being the world’s second-largest industry, construction remains one of the least digitalized, with only 30% of onsite time spent on actual building tasks. At Dalux, we’re changing this by providing end-to-end solutions that streamline the entire lifecycle of a building—from design and construction to maintenance and eventual demolition—reducing waste, time, and costs.

We stay ahead by using cutting-edge technology, including cloud solutions, drones, computer vision, and AI, to transform how the construction industry works. Over the last five years, we’ve grown by 60% annually and now have over 700 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

If you’re curious to learn more about Dalux and our products, feel free to visit our LinkedIn or website, where you can find videos and descriptions of our events, products, and the work we do.

About FPRT

FirePoint Rocket Technology is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark - a new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. Joining us now means becoming part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up.

The Role

As the Senior Process Engineer, you will be crucial in ensuring the stability, safety, and continuous improvement of FPRT's production processes. This role combines engineering, optimization, and practical design to ensure every manufacturing stage—from material preparation and mixing to polymerization and final assembly - operates efficiently, safely, and in line with company standards.

You will report to the Chief Production Officer (CPO).

What You Will Do

1. Process Documentation & Standardization

• 
Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all process steps, including mixing, polymerization, demolding, assembly, and testing.

• 
Observe real operations and translate them into clear, standardized, and safe work instructions.

• 
Ensure documentation aligns with HSE, ISO 9001, and defense manufacturing standards.

2. Process Optimization & Efficiency

• 
Analyze production workflows to identify manual or inefficient operations.

• 
Propose, design, or support the creation of mechanical tools, fixtures, or automated solutions that boost productivity and safety.

• 
Evaluate how existing machines and equipment are utilized; recommend modifications or redesigns for better efficiency.

• 
Apply Lean and PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) principles to reduce waste, rework, and downtime.

3. Equipment & Technical Design Support

• 
Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering on the development and fabrication of custom in-house equipment (e.g., mixing accessories, molds, handling systems, transport carts, fixtures).

• 
Prepare basic technical sketches or 3D models for small mechanical improvements or automation concepts.

• 
Support the setup, validation, and calibration of new or modified tools and machinery.

4. Process Monitoring & Validation

• 
Monitor process parameters (temperature, pressure, vacuum, timing) and ensure compliance with defined limits.

• 
Collect and analyze process data to detect trends, variations, or potential improvements.

• 
Support validation and certification activities under CPO supervision.

What We Offer

• 
A challenging role where you act as an in-house constructor-technologist by designing custom tools, jigs, trolleys, and mechanical aids that cannot be sourced externally.

• 
An opportunity to directly impact the safety and efficiency of a unique industrial and defense-tech project in Denmark.

• 
A collaborative professional environment where you will work closely with Chemical Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, and HSE teams.

• 
Top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

What We Are Looking For

You are an individual with an analytical mindset, creativity, and hands-on problem-solving ability, driven by a safety- and quality-focused attitude.

Education:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Process, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering.

Experience:

• Minimum 5 years in process or production engineering in manufacturing, preferably defense, aerospace, or chemical.

Expertise:

• 
Strong understanding of mechanical design, ergonomics, and process optimization.

• 
Experience in documenting and validating processes and equipment.

• 
Basic CAD or 3D modeling skills (e.g., SolidWorks, Inventor, or similar).

• 
Knowledge of HSE and ISO 9001 standards.

Security Clearance & Vetting Notice

Due to the sensitive defense-tech nature of our projects and operations, all potential employees are subject to a police and intelligence background check as part of our standard recruitment process. Continued employment is conditional upon obtaining and maintaining the necessary security clearance.
